body:
Security review of the server API (2026-09-19), finding 4 of 4. Low.

`POST /sync` accepts `full_lists` as any list of strings: no length cap and no deduplication. `delta` runs a full snapshot query pair per entry, so one authenticated member can send the same big list id thousands of times in one 4 MB request and multiply the read work (the response is deduplicated by dict, the queries are not). The row cap `too_many_changes` (T-114) only bounds pushes.

Fix: deduplicate (`set`) and cap `full_lists` — 250 entries, the same scale as MAX_CHANGES_PER_SYNC — answering `422 invalid_full_lists` above it (an existing code; no client change). Test: 251 entries rejected, duplicates collapsed to one query.
title: sync: deduplicate and cap full_lists
